valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 20 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a resort owner-operator in Sri Lanka and the Maldives (Cinnamon brand), one sector. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) can't be opened from this run (his site is blocked by the network settings). Stand-in: his global sector table, January 2026, Hotel/Gaming unlevered beta corrected for cash 0.66 (web-search extract), the same stand-in used for Aitken Spence Hotel Holdings. (3) Relevered with net debt Rs 33.28bn (30 Sep 2026: borrowings Rs 19.23bn + leases Rs 16.02bn − cash and short-term investments Rs 1.97bn) ÷ market value of equity Rs 23.74bn (Rs 16.30 × 1,456.15mn shares) = 1.40, tax 30%: 0.66 × (1 + 0.7 × 1.40) = 1.31. (4) Local 5-year betas: none found by web search on 20 Nov 2026, so step 4 can't be completed. (5) Higher of 1.31 and (no local figure) = 1.31. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with the emerging-markets file and three local 5-year betas.

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: The company doesn't split its capex between upkeep and expansion; it calls its capex 'recurring' (rooms, public areas, back of house). Right-of-use depreciation is left out because the lease liabilities are subtracted as debt.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: scripts/reinvestment.py: debt weight 58.4% (net debt Rs 33.28bn incl. leases, market cap Rs 23.74bn at Rs 16.30), cost of debt 6.31% (interest paid Rs 2.30bn ÷ average borrowings and leases, 2025/26; below the bond yield because much of the Maldives debt and leases are in dollars at SOFR-linked rates), tax 33.8% (2025/26 effective rate).

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 1% / 3% / 5% (next five years, rupees); supported -1.3% (reinvestment rate -26.9% × return on capital 5.0%, 2025/26). All more than 2 pts above.
valuationInputs.reason: Capex has been below depreciation for two years, so measured reinvestment is negative. The assumptions are in rupees and about 60% of revenue is the dollar-earning Maldives, so rupee depreciation and room-rate inflation lift cash without new rooms; start cash is already cut for the first-half shock; and the DCF still charges growth ÷ return on capital (5/7/9%) as reinvestment.

valuationInputs.name: DCF inputs
valuationInputs.value: Start cash Rs 4.1bn / 4.6bn / 5.6bn; NOPAT Rs 2.4bn / 2.9bn / 3.4bn; growth 1/3/5% then 2/3/4%; return on new capital 5/7/9%; upkeep capex Rs 2.51bn / 2.51bn / 1.45bn
valuationInputs.reason: 2025/26 start cash Rs 5.2bn (operating cash Rs 6.19bn + after-tax interest Rs 1.52bn − depreciation Rs 2.51bn); bear back to about 2024/25's level, base cut by about half the first half's Rs 1.3bn fall in operating profit. NOPAT from recurring operating profit Rs 4.0bn at about 25% tax (blend of 30% Sri Lanka and 15% Maldives). Leases are counted as debt, so right-of-use depreciation is left out of upkeep.

valuationInputs.name: Normalised EPS × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: 2025/26 EPS Rs 1.33 included about Rs 0.53 from the Kandy sale (after capital gains tax) and Rs 0.26 of investment-property gain; recurring about Rs 0.55–0.62. Next-year EPS isn't used because the half-year loss (Rs 1.64) makes it near zero or negative.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE (price to book)
valuationInputs.reason: Ten-year ROE: 7.8% (2016/17) at best, losses 2020/21–2024/25, 5.9% in 2025/26 with one-offs, about 2.5% without.

valuationInputs.name: NAV multiple
valuationInputs.reason: ROE far below the cost of equity; the share traded at 0.34–0.93x NAV at March year ends over ten years.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: NAV multiple, whole-company DCF, justified P/E on normalised EPS, justified price to book
valuationInputs.reason: Residual income left out (it repeats price to book here); dividend too small and irregular for a dividend model.

openQuestions: Q3 (to December 2026, due early December): does the peak season bring the Maldives back to profit, and is nine-month EPS better than last year's Rs -0.48?
Does net debt including leases fall back below equity by March 2027 (Rs 33.3bn against Rs 32.9bn at September)?
Cinnamon Wild Yala: is the refurbishment on time for Q4 2026/27, and what did it cost?
Where do the Kandy proceeds go: capex (Rs 0.53bn in the half, less than last year) or debt?
Annual report 2026/27: record capex booked, depreciation, interest paid and any company split of maintenance capex; check whether capex stays below depreciation.
Beta: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets Hotel/Gaming figure and three local 5-year betas. Price: replace the 30 Sep 2026 last trade with the CSE close.

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add KHL.N0000). First analysis from the 2025/26 annual report and the interims to June and September 2026. Price Rs 16.30 is the last trade on 30 Sep 2026 from the interim report: the CSE close wasn't available (KHL not yet in generated/prices.json; CSE and price sites blocked from this run). Beta 1.31 provisional (Damodaran global Hotel/Gaming 0.66, relevered; no local 5-year betas found). Methods: NAV multiple, whole-company DCF, justified P/E on normalised EPS, justified price to book. Business tests 1/4, category 3. Fair value Rs 5.94, buy Rs 5.05, strong buy Rs 4.46.
